FirstLight doubles capacity at former NATO data center in Maine

profile.research_note: Additional detail per Data Center Dynamics: facility (14 Resilient Circle, Brunswick Landing) is a former NATO Command and Control Center at the decommissioned Brunswick Naval Air Station, launched as a commercial facility ~2011, acquired by FirstLight ~2017 via the Oxford Networks merger (explains "Oxford Networks" name on this DB row). Power capacity doubled in a 2024 renovation: dual independent 750kW generators (1.5MW standby, stored). Rack density reported as 12-15kW/rack for liquid-cooled racks -- a range, not stored as a single power_density figure per policy. No IT capacity (critical load) or sqft figure published.

reading.body:
Oxford Networks, a data center in Brunswick, Maine now operated by FirstLight, has no published capacity or square footage data in available sources.

The facility exists as a mapped location but remains opaque to public measurement. The operator's website structure has changed since this facility was last documented, and the specific product page now returns a 404 error. No alternative official sources list capacity, power draw, or building specifications for this site.

This illustrates a broader problem in tracking data center infrastructure for compute capacity: operator websites are often the only public source for facility specs, those sites change without preserving historical URLs, and many operators do not publish detailed technical information even for active facilities. Without this data, estimating Maine's data center power footprint or computing capacity becomes speculative.
